programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing airson an itealaig aige a sgèith gun chuideachadh bho dhuine sam bith – fiù 's a charaid Pando. Ge-tà, nuair a thig cùisean ceàrr 's ann a tha Bing ag ionnsachadh cho feumail 's a tha beagan taic! Bing wants to fly his kite all by himself and doesn't want to accept help from anyone, not even his good friend Pando. However, when things get a bit tangled up, Bing realises the importance of a helping hand!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing san amar 's e airson an t-uabhas bhuilgeanan a chruthachadh le bhith cur barrachd 's barrachd stuth bhuilgean dhan uisge. Ge-tà chan eil fad ann gus am bi tuilleadh 's còrr a bhuilgeanan ga chuartachadh…! It's Bing's bath time and he's keen to create as many bubbles as possible by adding more and more bubble goo to the water. However, there are soon too many bubbles for Bing to handle!

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha e a' còrdadh ri na h-Abadas a bhith a' cluich le bàll air a' chladach, gus a bheil gaoth làidir a' sèideadh am bàll a-muigh gu muir! Tha na h-Abadas ag ionnsachadh nach e 'bàll' an aon rud a bhios a' gluasad sa ghaoth. The Abadas are enjoying a game of ball at the seaside until the strong winds blow the ball out to sea! The Abadas soon find out that a ball isn't the only thing that moves in the wind.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Àtaidh a’ cur èisg ghleansach ris a’ chruinneachadh aige, ach chan fhada gus an tuig e gu bheil iad a’ toirt suas barrachd rùm na bha e an dùil. Nise càit’ an cadail e? Abney adds some shiny fish to his collection but soon finds that they take up more room than expected. Now where can he get some sleep?

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha fear de dheargannan Theàrlaich a’ bìdeadh Pheicein, is an uair sin tha e fhèin is a charaidean a’ cruthachadh sreath-bìdh le seangain, mosgìotothan is damhain-àlaidh mhòra airson cuidhteas fhaighinn dhe na deargannan air fad. Petit gets bitten by one of Tadeo's fleas. He and his friends decide to create a food chain, from ants to mosquitoes to tarantulas, and get rid of the fleas once and for all.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Babs Nicgriogair a’ leughadh Slighe Dhraoidheil Matisse. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Tim Hopgood, a dhealbhachadh le Sam Boughton agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Babs Macgregor reads Slighe Dhraoidheil Matisse, written by Tim Hopgood, illustrated by Sam Boughton and translated into Gaelic by Jo MacDonald.

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Mar is àbhaist, tha nàmhaid nan Neachdan, Alpheus Benthos, a’ feuchainn ris an Ephemychron a ghoid bhuapa is an stad bho Lemuria a lorg. The nemesis of the Neachdan, Alpheus Benthos, is as usual trying to steal the Ephemychron and prevent them from finding Lemuria.

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Nuair a tha an Alien, seann charaid Sheonaidh, a' cur feum air an taigh-bheag a chleachdadh, tha Seonaidh ro dheònach gun cleachd e na goireasan aige! Fhad 's a tha e a-muigh, tha e a' fàgail Seonaidh an urra ris an inneal leusair....ach tha fhios nach bi làmhan Sheonaidh nan tàmh! When Shaun's old friend the alien drops by for much-needed loo break, Shaun is only too happy to let him use the facilities in the farmhouse. While he's going about his business, he leaves Shaun in charge of his intriguing new gadget. Can Shaun resist the urge to give it a go? Of course not!

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Sombaidh Ceitidh a’ gabhail fear de shiùcairean Granaidh, is tha bhlas cho làidir is gu bheil e a’ cur a h-anam beò aiste. Feumaidh Pòl is a charaidean feuchainn ri h-anam beò a thilleadh air ais na bodhaig, mus bheil e ro anmoch. Zombie Katie is so shocked by the taste of one of Gran’s Fishermen’s Enemy sweets that her life force leaves her body. Dave and his friends need to find Katie’s naughty life force before it is too late.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Gun fhiosta dha, tha Pòl a’ dèanamh toll ann am fànas agus feumaidh e feuchainn ri dòigh fhaighinn air a chàradh mus tèid gach nì a tharraing a-steach dhan toll mhòr dhubh. Dave accidentally rips the fabric of space and must find a way to fix it before the whole universe gets sucked inside the black hole beyond.

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra
programme.desc: Mairi Rodgers explores Kailzie Gardens near Peebles. Tha Màiri Rodgers a’ gabhail cuairt tro Ghàrraidhean Kailzie faisg air na Pùballan.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Climber Kenny Rankin, who grew up in Lochalsh, pops in, and Calum Maclean is in Uddingston trying his hand at a sport he last played in primary school.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Fuine
programme.desc: Gregor MacLeod learns about a recipe book from 100 years ago that has been kept in the family.

programme.title: Luchd-Brathaidh Cogaidh | Spies of War
programme.desc: Ionnsaich mar a mheall àidseantan dùbailte MI5 na Gearmailtich gus na feachdan aca a chumail fad air falbh bho Normandy. How MI5 double agents tricked the Germans over D-Day.

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le Sgoil Chiùil na Gàidhealtachd agus Hadhirgaan, clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads, 2025. A’ gabhail a-steach Fisherrow Set agus Netherbow Set. Concert set performed by Sgoil Chiùil na Gàidhealtachd and Hadhirgaan, recorded live at the Trad Awards, 2025. Featured tracks include Fisherrow Set and Netherbow Set.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Leis gu bheil e a-nis slàn, fallain às dèidh ionnsachadh bho chionn còrr is bliadhna gu bheil a chridhe a’ fàiligeadh, tha Ruairidh, cuide ri Ùisdean, ag ullachadh measgachadh de shoithichean mar dhòigh taing a thoirt do dhithis dhen na nursaichean a bh’ aige. Tha Ruairidh a’ dèanamh Bonnaich Crùbaig Baltimore, Pàidh Ùbhlan gun Siùcar no Bathar-bainne, airson a ghabhail le Reòiteag gun Bhathar-bainne. Tha Ùisdean, a tha cinnteach gu bheil feum aig Ruairidh air pàirtean a bharrachd, a’ dèanamh Cridhe Daimh air a lìonadh le Càl-bloinigein agus Duxelles Balgain-buachrach. Tha e cuideachd a’ dèanamh soitheach blasta le Breac-garbh agus Beurre Blanc. Having thankfully been given a clean bill of health after Roddy's heart failure diagnosis over a year ago, he and Uisdean prepare a selection of dishes as a small thank you to two of his nurses. Roddy prepares Baltimore crab cakes, a dairy and sugar-free apple pie to be accompanied with dairy-free ice cream! Uisdean, convinced that Roddy might need a spare part, prepares ox heart stuffed with spinach and mushroom duxelles. For a tasty fish dish, he cooks up halibut with Bleurre blanc. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Beloved Wilderness
programme.desc: Documentary examining the work of the Highlands and Islands Development Board during the 1960s, originally aired in 1970.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: ’S e a’ chiad latha de Belladrum 2025 a th’ ann agus tha Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilt’ air gaisgich indie rock, The Pigeon Detectives, gu Àrd-Ùrlar a’ Ghàrraidh. Air an stèidheachadh ann an 2004 ann an Rothwell, Leeds, tha an còmhlan air iad fhèin a dhearbhadh aig na fèisean agus tha e furasta fhaicinn carson, le òrain ceòlmhor mar ‘I Found Out’ agus ‘Take Her Back’. It’s the first day at Belladrum 2025, and Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald welcome indie rock heroes The Pigeon Detectives to the Garden Stage. Formed in 2004 in Rothwell, Leeds, the band have established themselves as festival favourites, and it’s easy to see why with singalong hits such as I Found Out and Take Her Back.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Tha ceangal làidir aig an sgìre Costa Blanca san Spàinn ri saor-làithean is luchd-turais a’ sireadh na grèine, ach tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ faighinn a-mach gu bheil an sgìre seo a’ tabhann sreap air leth don neach-siubhal as Dàna. Còmhla ris a’ chompanach sreap, Somhairle Mac Iain, tha Coinneach a’ cur seachad ùine ann an aon de na cinn-uidhe turasachd as motha san Roinn Eòrpa agus a’ tighinn tarsaing air dùbhlain inntinneach air a’ bhlàr a-muigh, air falbh bho ghleadhraich Baile Benidorm. While Spain’s Costa Blanca may be more closely associated with package holidays than with adventure sports, Coinneach Rankin finds that the area offers incredible climbing to the more intrepid holidaymaker. Along with climbing partner, Somhairle Johnston, Coinneach explores one of Europe’s most popular tourist destinations and discovers thrilling challenges, a world apart from the bustle of Benidorm. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: The Hadron Collider: In Search of the Peace Particle
programme.desc: In the aftermath of Hiroshima, a group of scientists vowed never to turn knowledge into weapons again, and from that promise, CERN was born. Deep underground, researchers from nations in conflict have worked side by side for decades, driven by curiosity and shared wonder. For 70 years, CERN has stood as an act of hope, a place where collaboration transcends borders, even as the world above grows more divided. Blending poetry, music and rare archival footage of nuclear physicist Robert Oppenheimer with remarkable access to the Large Hadron Collider, the film explores how science, politics and culture collide.

programme.title: Little Ships: The Miracle of Dunkirk
programme.desc: To mark the 70th anniversary of the 'miracle of Dunkirk', 50 of the surviving 'little ships' that made the original perilous cross-channel voyage are returning to France. Dan Snow tells their extraordinary story: their role in the evacuation and the people who struggled to keep them afloat during those fateful days in 1940, when the future of Europe hung in the balance.

programme.title: The Smuggling Business: Undercover
programme.desc: Over the past two years, tens of thousands of migrants have crossed the English Channel in small boats from northern France, despite repeated promises by successive governments to stop the trade. This undercover BBC investigation reveals how people smuggling gangs are operating in plain sight inside a migrant camp in Dunkirk. It exposes a highly organised criminal marketplace driven by fierce competition between rival groups, who enforce control over the settlements through fear, violence and intimidation. The film examines efforts by UK authorities to disrupt and dismantle the criminal networks profiting from the crossings, and questions whether those measures are keeping pace with the scale and sophistication of the operation. BBC investigative reporter Josie Hannett also travels to Crowborough, where opposition to a new asylum seeker accommodation site has turned the town into a flashpoint in the national immigration debate. She asks whether current government policy is likely to deter future arrivals, or whether the UK is preparing for a future that will require many more such sites across the south east

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin encounters a Grade II listed property in Wiltshire with a dodgy-looking extension that the new owner will surely have to rectify. Owain is in north London, where he falls in love with the mid-century charm of a terraced house. Jacqui is in Wembley looking around a tidy little flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: There are plenty of goodies that the teams can buy in this episode from Derbyshire, but the one thing they can’t buy is more time! Sixty minutes is all they get - but back at the turn of the 20th century you could buy time - from the Greenwich Time Lady! Natasha Raskin Sharp tells the fascinating story of Ruth Belville who walked the streets of London, ‘selling’ the time to local businesses.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The Garden of England is calling as a young couple from Greater London head deeper into the Kent countryside in search of more space and fresh air for them and their two young children. Guiding them every step of the way is Nicki Chapman, who has some stunning family homes in her line-up, including an epic medieval mystery house packed with wow factor. Nicki’s day gets even brighter when she meets a local flower farmer bringing more bursts of colour and beautiful bouquets to the Kent countryside.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Lee are in Epsom to convert Jade and Jack’s long, plain and unkempt garden into a sporty socialising space. Both are from avid sports-loving families. They would love a bar area to watch live football games, a place to host friends and chill, and a space to play competitive darts, football and bowls! Can the team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mo, Hannah, Rich and Nathan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mo, Hannah, Rich and Nathan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When a group of odd-job workmen turn up at Linda’s 87-year-old father's house saying he needs work doing, she races over before he parts with potentially hundreds of pounds. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gets his hands dirty as he shows how our rubbish can be a treasure trove for criminals. And Matt speaks to a man who chased down a gang of suspected car thieves all by himself.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin encounters a Grade II listed property in Wiltshire with a dodgy-looking extension that the new owner will surely have to rectify. Owain is in north London, where he falls in love with the mid-century charm of a terraced house. Jacqui is in Wembley looking around a tidy little flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: There are plenty of goodies that the teams can buy in this episode from Derbyshire, but the one thing they can’t buy is more time! Sixty minutes is all they get - but back at the turn of the 20th century you could buy time - from the Greenwich Time Lady! Natasha Raskin Sharp tells the fascinating story of Ruth Belville who walked the streets of London, ‘selling’ the time to local businesses.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: England football legend Steph Houghton joins Robson at Crag Pond in Teesdale for some outdoor activities. He takes the former Lioness tree climbing and canoeing before signing them up for bush craft, where they learn how to light a fire with sticks and eat a campfire supper. Later, Robson heads into Upper Swaledale in North Yorkshire for a waterfall swim and sauna.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The Garden of England is calling as a young couple from Greater London head deeper into the Kent countryside in search of more space and fresh air for them and their two young children. Guiding them every step of the way is Nicki Chapman, who has some stunning family homes in her line-up, including an epic medieval mystery house packed with wow factor. Nicki’s day gets even brighter when she meets a local flower farmer bringing more bursts of colour and beautiful bouquets to the Kent countryside.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Lee are in Epsom to convert Jade and Jack’s long, plain and unkempt garden into a sporty socialising space. Both are from avid sports-loving families. They would love a bar area to watch live football games, a place to host friends and chill, and a space to play competitive darts, football and bowls! Can the team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mo, Hannah, Rich and Nathan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Ria Lina for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

Guiding them every step of the way is Nicki Chapman, who has some stunning family homes in her line-up, including an epic medieval mystery house packed with wow factor. Nicki’s day gets even brighter when she meets a local flower farmer bringing more bursts of colour and beautiful bouquets to the Kent countryside.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Lee are in Epsom to convert Jade and Jack’s long, plain and unkempt garden into a sporty socialising space. Both are from avid sports-loving families. They would love a bar area to watch live football games, a place to host friends and chill, and a space to play competitive darts, football and bowls! Can the team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mo, Hannah, Rich and Nathan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin encounters a Grade II listed property in Wiltshire with a dodgy-looking extension that the new owner will surely have to rectify. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: There are plenty of goodies that the teams can buy in this episode from Derbyshire, but the one thing they can’t buy is more time! Sixty minutes is all they get - but back at the turn of the 20th century you could buy time - from the Greenwich Time Lady! Natasha Raskin Sharp tells the fascinating story of Ruth Belville who walked the streets of London, ‘selling’ the time to local businesses.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When a group of odd-job workmen turn up at Linda’s 87-year-old father's house saying he needs work doing, she races over before he parts with potentially hundreds of pounds. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gets his hands dirty as he shows how our rubbish can be a treasure trove for criminals. And Matt speaks to a man who chased down a gang of suspected car thieves all by himself.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin encounters a Grade II listed property in Wiltshire with a dodgy-looking extension that the new owner will surely have to rectify. Owain is in north London, where he falls in love with the mid-century charm of a terraced house. Jacqui is in Wembley looking around a tidy little flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: There are plenty of goodies that the teams can buy in this episode from Derbyshire, but the one thing they can’t buy is more time! Sixty minutes is all they get - but back at the turn of the 20th century you could buy time - from the Greenwich Time Lady! Natasha Raskin Sharp tells the fascinating story of Ruth Belville who walked the streets of London, ‘selling’ the time to local businesses.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: As Natalie faces her final test, hospice care, reflection and a visit to Belfast show this journey may just be beginning.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: England football legend Steph Houghton joins Robson at Crag Pond in Teesdale for some outdoor activities. He takes the former Lioness tree climbing and canoeing before signing them up for bush craft, where they learn how to light a fire with sticks and eat a campfire supper. Later, Robson heads into Upper Swaledale in North Yorkshire for a waterfall swim and sauna.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The Garden of England is calling as a young couple from Greater London head deeper into the Kent countryside in search of more space and fresh air for them and their two young children. Guiding them every step of the way is Nicki Chapman, who has some stunning family homes in her line-up, including an epic medieval mystery house packed with wow factor. Nicki’s day gets even brighter when she meets a local flower farmer bringing more bursts of colour and beautiful bouquets to the Kent countryside.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Lee are in Epsom to convert Jade and Jack’s long, plain and unkempt garden into a sporty socialising space. Both are from avid sports-loving families. They would love a bar area to watch live football games, a place to host friends and chill, and a space to play competitive darts, football and bowls! Can the team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mo, Hannah, Rich and Nathan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Ria Lina for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.desc: England football legend Steph Houghton joins Robson at Crag Pond in Teesdale for some outdoor activities. He takes the former Lioness tree climbing and canoeing before signing them up for bush craft, where they learn how to light a fire with sticks and eat a campfire supper. programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The Garden of England is calling as a young couple from Greater London head deeper into the Kent countryside in search of more space and fresh air for them and their two young children. Guiding them every step of the way is Nicki Chapman, who has some stunning family homes in her line-up, including an epic medieval mystery house packed with wow factor. Nicki’s day gets even brighter when she meets a local flower farmer bringing more bursts of colour and beautiful bouquets to the Kent countryside.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Lee are in Epsom to convert Jade and Jack’s long, plain and unkempt garden into a sporty socialising space. Both are from avid sports-loving families. They would love a bar area to watch live football games, a place to host friends and chill, and a space to play competitive darts, football and bowls! Can the team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mo, Hannah, Rich and Nathan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: Paul Murton explores the River Garry and hears tales of clan chief Struan Robertson, who fought in all three Jacobite risings. Paul then discovers the geology of deep time, before restaging the Battle of Killiecrankie with just two men, a musket and a broadsword. After surviving a Highland charge, Paul falls off a bridge. He reaches journey’s end on the beautiful Ben Vrackie - the ‘speckled hill’.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Sound advice for everyday gardening from Brian Cunningham and Calum Clunie at Beechgrove. Calum is planting up hanging baskets, a great way to decorate a doorstep or shed, and talks about his favourite bedding plants to get planted right now. Brian demonstrates the best way to tackle a border that has gotten out of control and what you should be doing with some of your rhododendrons at this time of year. Calum is busy in his family plot at Beechgrove as he shows just what can be done in an average-sized garden, and also in his competition plot, where he has been challenged to cultivate a border full of scent. There is a report from one of the show’s regular contributors and their allotment in Perth, along with all the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie is in Rogart, a vibrant crofting community in East Sutherland, where he finds out about the challenges in modern crofting. Meanwhile, Shahbaz takes a walk to the Bone Caves near Inchnadamph to see how an increase in visitor numbers is damaging the site. Leanna visits a pond in the grounds of Castle Fraser in Aberdeenshire that’s become a haven for rare damselflies and dragonflies. Rosie is in Assynt to discover what is being done to protect some of the UK's last surviving elm trees. Meanwhile, Cammy is in Dumfrieshire to meet a young dairy farmer who got her big break into the industry via a unique opportunity.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: Police race to a tragic accident on the A9, one of the Highlands’ busiest and most dangerous roads. In Fort William, PCs Roddy Sandeman and Stephen Cooper are on the hunt for a man who has evaded capture for months and believe he might be hiding on the dark, tree-lined banks of Loch Ailort. And police in Inverness intercept drug packages sent through the post.

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: A portrait of journalist Chick Young, who has been a familiar voice and face in Scottish football for more than five decades

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Gordon's parents Graham and Sandra visit Scotland from Yorkshire and Ian and Gordon bring them to Latimer Crescent to meet Beth and Eric. Christine turns up with her own take on the Scottish attractions to visit, at which point Ian and Gordon grab the opportunity to pop out for some herbal tea for Sandra. When they get back, Cathy and Colin have arrived after sensing there may be the chance of a drink, and the chat has turned to further delights for visitors to Scotland. And the men step outside to admire Graham's beautifully restored vintage car. Despite the interference of the unexpected guests, the tea party is all going rather well until the conversation turns to Scotland's sporting successes.

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Conversation about Scotland’s biggest news stories, hosted by Martin Geissler.

programme.title: Life on the Bay
programme.desc: The sun continues to shine on the 600 caravans overlooking the Firth of Forth, on the Fife coast. After many months of restrictions, the team are excited to be bring back live entertainment for the residents and renters of the park’s 600 caravans. Bar and restaurant manager Blythe has great news for one caravan park veteran eager to get his quiz night up and running. Meanwhile, children and their parents are treated to a magic show, and maintenance team member Mark prepares for his wedding in the park’s hotel, with a live performance from one talented caravan resident.

programme.title: Loop
programme.desc: For the past year, artist Hannah Imlach has been designing and building the ‘Moth Kota’, an experimental structure designed to allow humans to have an ethical encounter with moths on the RSPB Loch Lomond Reserve. Topped by an ultraviolet sphere, it attracts moths inside, where the nocturnal creatures can be observed and a record kept of the species present on the site before they are released.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Wildlife expert Steve Backshall meets one of the planet's ultimate killers, the saltwater crocodile, as the Deadly 60 team land in Australia's Northern Territories. A rogue croc is terrorising local fisherman, so it is time to lend the park rangers a hand in catching and relocating this prehistoric monster. Steve heads deep into an abandoned mine on a ghost hunt. He is on the search for ghost bats, awesome creatures with huge fangs, that drop on to their prey out of the night sky. Scary stuff, and a first for the Deadly team as these bats have never been filmed in the wild before.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall heads to a place very few people ever go: Snake Island in Brazil, where the concentration of snakes is higher than anywhere else on earth.

programme.title: Athletics: Diamond League
programme.desc: World-class athletics from the Eternal City as a plethora of household names in track and field compete at the Stadio Olimpico in the fourth Diamond League meet of the season.

programme.title: Kidnapped by My Mum
programme.desc: At 11 years old, Alex vanished on holiday with his mother and grandfather for six years. Now, he's retracing his steps across Europe to tell the full story for the first time.

programme.title: Ladhood
programme.desc: Liam has instigated yet another confrontation with a stranger in a bar, for the crime of having a conversation with his girlfriend, Jess. Before the altercation reaches fever pitch, Liam delves into the memories of his adolescence and questions where this toxic behaviour stems from. Leeds, early noughties. On the last day of the school year one of Liam’s best mates, Ralph, sees Rachel flirting with Whitey, the hardest lad in school. Ralph threatens (under his breath) to 'smack him'. Word of the threat gets back to Whitey’s friends, Rupert and Tinhead, who organise a fight between Ralph and Whitey for the following Friday. Ralph can’t win and he knows it. In a panic, he considers staying home all summer. But Rupert and Tinhead tell Liam that if Ralph doesn’t show, they’ll hunt Liam down and batter him instead. Back in the present day, Liam crosses the bar towards the man he’s been arguing with.

programme.title: Ladhood
programme.desc: Having previously embarrassing himself in a bar, Liam announces to his girlfriend, Jess, that he’s taking a month off the booze. As he tries to make it through his first sober Friday night in years, he thinks back to where and when his relationship with drinking began. Leeds, early noughties. It’s Friday night and Liam, Ralph, Addy and Craggy are determined to get drunk for the first time. The only problem is, they’re underage. Trying every trick in the book to get served, they find unlikely heroes in local bullies Rupert and Tinhead, who agree to buy their booze. But when Rupert invites them to the woods for a drinking session, things get messy.

programme.title: Ladhood
programme.desc: After a bad day at work, Liam is forced to finally confront his mental health problems. When Jess suggests he should go for therapy, Liam recalls the last time he received this advice. Leeds, early noughties. As a disillusioned teenager, Liam regularly takes his aggression out on school bins. He finds little emotional support from PE teacher, and traditional man’s man, Mr Stones. But when an unconventional substitute teacher named Miss Monroe appears, Liam tries to channel his anger into more creative pursuits.

programme.title: Dubai Hustle
programme.desc: The Brokers are back! Adam and Jake try to impress an influential client, new boy Eddie attempts to become a millionaire investor’s exclusive agent, and Chris is under scrutiny.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: In the second part of the Top Gear special, Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May continue their epic African odyssey. Having survived insane traffic, lethal mudslides and some distinctly dubious map reading, the trio and their ailing estate cars reach the climax of their quest to find the definitive source of the Nile.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Celebrity players Nitin Ganatra, the Rev Kate Bottley and Alex Gray, aka Apollo from Gladiators, face another knowledge battle, led by Vernon Kay and aided by unreliable tour guide Paul Gorton. It's the halfway point, and the gloves are off for today’s destination, Falkirk.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In glorious Gloucestershire, Nicki Chapman helps Peggy finally make her long-awaited escape from London. After years of dreaming, she’s ready to find a home that suits her and her crew – two dogs and a horse called Tom. Emotions are running high as Nicki lines up a selection of spectacular properties from where some of the county’s amazing views can be seen. Nicki also meets a pair of street food chefs who have swapped the city buzz for a slice of country living.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Continuing his Belgian tour, Michael Portillo heads to the beach resort of Knokke-Heist and the world’s longest coastal tram, which enjoys splendid views across the North Sea, to trace its roots back to the 19th-century beginnings of tourism. He visits the Port of Zeebrugge, which was attacked by the British in 1918 when the country was occupied by the Germans. Further along the coast on the Dutch border, Michael explores the salt marshes and mud flats of the Zwin Nature Reserve, home to 300 species of birds, and helps to track their migration habits. And continuing to the medieval city of Bruges, Michael visits a saxophone maker and discovers how the instrument, so crucial to the development of jazz, was invented in Belgium.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With summer just around the corner, Monty is bringing bold colour to the garden, planting gingers and cannas, setting out tomatoes and sowing wallflowers straight into the soil. From her Devon garden, Carol Klein is exploring the latest plant science, uncovering what is really going on inside a seed the moment it is sown, and how this pioneering knowledge can transform the way people garden. Rekha Mistry is also on a mission to grow big in a small space, using only pots on her patio. In Oxfordshire, a garden designed for both beauty and biodiversity shows how plants can support wildlife as well as people. And a viewer in rural France shares a breathtaking, naturalistic plot that blends seamlessly with the surrounding landscape.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The quiz show where players must avoid Impossible answers to stay in the competition. 18 people start today’s show, but how many of them will survive to face the £10,000 question?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents another heat of a new series of the classic quiz where contenders take on the famous black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. Tonight's specialist subjects are the films of Nicole Kidman, constellations of the northern hemisphere, the children's books of Roald Dahl and Take That.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The Mackay family want to make the most of the sunny spot in an unloved corner of the garden in their London home. Their shed is tired and so full they can’t fit anything in, and their bathroom is showing signs of age and limescale. The team construct decking and a pergola so the family can enjoy the sunshine together. The shed is tidied with storage added, and their bathroom is deep cleaned so it gleams.

programme.title: The Great British Countryside
programme.desc: Hugh Dennis and Julia Bradbury are in the Highlands of Scotland, Britain's wildest and oldest landscape. They explore a landscape built by volcanoes, earthquakes and ice.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: From the sublime to the ridiculous - a painting by an Australian war artist, a silver claret jug and two diamond rings contrast with a painting with a large hole through the middle and a permit for carrying a cigarette lighter in Portugal. Michael and the experts visit Leeds Town Hall.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the historic Barrow Hill Roundhouse near Chesterfield in Derbyshire, where experts Jonathan Pratt and Michael Baggott value some of the county's antiques and collectibles. Jonathan falls in love with a Thonet hat and coat stand, and Michael comes across a box of Victorian cut-throat razors which get pulses racing at the auction. Paul Martin takes a trip to the village of Hathersage in the Peak District National Park, which provided inspiration for the novel Jane Eyre.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Nikki Fox, Ruthie Henshall, Danny John-Jules and Ignacio Lopez take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Belgian journey takes him back to Brussels to examine a dark chapter in the country’s past. At the Museum of Africa, on the edge of the city, he learns about Belgium’s brutal seizure of the Congo under King Leopold II and a grand exhibition to celebrate his colonial success. Travelling south into French-speaking Wallonia, Michael visits the site of the Battle of Waterloo, one of Britain’s most famous military victories. He explores a key position at Hougoumont Farm, where Wellington’s soldiers defended themselves from Napoleon’s forces, and joins re-enactors to fire a cannon known as Le Brutal. In the province of Hainaut, the centre of Belgium’s Industrial Revolution, Michael admires a 19th-century boat lift, one of four on the Canal du Centre, the only working examples of their kind in the world today.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 1 highlights from the Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: As the second week of Springwatch draws to a close, Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan continue to uncover the remarkable wildlife stories unfolding at Crom, the beautiful reserve cared for by the National Trust. A mammal medley takes centre stage, with appearances from the pine marten, red squirrel and badger, whilst many of the chicks being monitored on the live cameras are beginning to fledge. Meanwhile, Iolo Williams wraps up his London adventure in Ealing, where local communities and conservation groups are working hard to restore wildlife and bring nature back into the urban landscape.

programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: On 17 August 1996, 21-year-old David Beckham raised his hands to the sky, having just scored against Wimbledon from his own half. That iconic image turned Beckham into a household name and kickstarted a relationship with image-making that would propel the footballer into the popular imagination and help redefine modern celebrity. But behind the popular narrative is a deeper story: of how the footballer used his image to turn himself into a global brand – one that went far beyond the limits of his extraordinary footballing skills – and in so doing helped change attitudes to celebrity, masculinity and class.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Officers attending a call to a house where a woman has been punched in the face are confronted by a man with a large knife. There is a tense stand-off before they are able to cuff and arrest him. Stephen challenges a man arrested for a hate-motivated crime close to Belfast city centre. There are comical scenes as the Peelers try to herd cattle through the busy streets of west Belfast. Back in the city centre, Dave and Owen come across a group of drug users openly injecting cocaine in broad daylight, in a public square. As they arrive, they find one man still injecting. A tense stand-off ensues, and police describe how they have to deal with the drug abuse and homelessness crisis. Elsewhere, officers are called to reports of a street fight between two women. While the police are trying to establish order amid the chaos, one woman wrestles with them, biting Anna and spitting blood into Tom and Adam’s eyes. She’s taken into custody wearing a spit and bite guard. Stephen looks on as the visibly distressed woman is processed through the police system. He is deeply affected by what he sees and hears – the reality of frontline policing.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Faisal Islam.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: A surgeon must remove his patient’s voice box to save his life, while another takes on a life-changing procedure for a patient with a rare auto-immune condition.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: The semi-finals continue, and just seven extraordinary home cooks remain in the competition. It’s time for them to dig even deeper into their culinary books of tricks.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Hannah explores whether the death of privacy puts society at greater risk or could make people safer.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: As the second week of Springwatch draws to a close, Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan continue to uncover the remarkable wildlife stories unfolding at Crom, the beautiful reserve cared for by the National Trust. A mammal medley takes centre stage, with appearances from the pine marten, red squirrel and badger, whilst many of the chicks being monitored on the live cameras are beginning to fledge. Meanwhile, Iolo Williams wraps up his London adventure in Ealing, where local communities and conservation groups are working hard to restore wildlife and bring nature back into the urban landscape.

programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: On 17 August 1996, 21-year-old David Beckham raised his hands to the sky, having just scored against Wimbledon from his own half. That iconic image turned Beckham into a household name and kickstarted a relationship with image-making that would propel the footballer into the popular imagination and help redefine modern celebrity. But behind the popular narrative is a deeper story: of how the footballer used his image to turn himself into a global brand – one that went far beyond the limits of his extraordinary footballing skills – and in so doing helped change attitudes to celebrity, masculinity and class.

programme.title: Carl Frampton - On Probation
programme.desc: Having heard the perspectives of probation staff and their service users, the last episode of the series sees Carl focus on the organisation’s role when it comes to liaising directly with victims of crime. Carl meets a young woman rebuilding her life after a violent crime. In an extraordinary turn of events, she embarks on a journey to meet the man she put behind bars to ask him questions that have been brewing since his actions changed her life. Carl also meets a man who ended up in Maghaberry Prison after funding his gambling addiction by controlling prostitution.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Faisal Islam.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Officers attending a call to a house where a woman has been punched in the face are confronted by a man with a large knife. There is a tense stand-off before they are able to cuff and arrest him. Stephen challenges a man arrested for a hate-motivated crime close to Belfast city centre. There are comical scenes as the Peelers try to herd cattle through the busy streets of west Belfast. Back in the city centre, Dave and Owen come across a group of drug users openly injecting cocaine in broad daylight, in a public square. As they arrive, they find one man still injecting. A tense stand-off ensues, and police describe how they have to deal with the drug abuse and homelessness crisis. Elsewhere, officers are called to reports of a street fight between two women. While the police are trying to establish order amid the chaos, one woman wrestles with them, biting Anna and spitting blood into Tom and Adam’s eyes. She’s taken into custody wearing a spit and bite guard. Stephen looks on as the visibly distressed woman is processed through the police system. He is deeply affected by what he sees and hears – the reality of frontline policing.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob head to the beautiful River Ouse in the heart of Bedfordshire. The river was once famous for barbel, but has recently become renowned for its big perch instead, a fish that has so far eluded them. After a long day fishing under the summer sun on the Turvey estate, Bob prepares a dinner that Paul will never forget - slow-cooked tripe.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: The semi-finals continue, and just seven extraordinary home cooks remain in the competition. It’s time for them to dig even deeper into their culinary books of tricks.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Hannah explores whether the death of privacy puts society at greater risk or could make people safer.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Celebrity players Nitin Ganatra, the Rev Kate Bottley and Alex Gray, aka Apollo from Gladiators, face another knowledge battle, led by Vernon Kay and aided by unreliable tour guide Paul Gorton. It's the halfway point, and the gloves are off for today’s destination, Falkirk.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In glorious Gloucestershire, Nicki Chapman helps Peggy finally make her long-awaited escape from London. After years of dreaming, she’s ready to find a home that suits her and her crew – two dogs and a horse called Tom. Emotions are running high as Nicki lines up a selection of spectacular properties from where some of the county’s amazing views can be seen. Nicki also meets a pair of street food chefs who have swapped the city buzz for a slice of country living.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Continuing his Belgian tour, Michael Portillo heads to the beach resort of Knokke-Heist and the world’s longest coastal tram, which enjoys splendid views across the North Sea, to trace its roots back to the 19th-century beginnings of tourism. He visits the Port of Zeebrugge, which was attacked by the British in 1918 when the country was occupied by the Germans. Further along the coast on the Dutch border, Michael explores the salt marshes and mud flats of the Zwin Nature Reserve, home to 300 species of birds, and helps to track their migration habits. And continuing to the medieval city of Bruges, Michael visits a saxophone maker and discovers how the instrument, so crucial to the development of jazz, was invented in Belgium.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With summer just around the corner, Monty is bringing bold colour to the garden, planting gingers and cannas, setting out tomatoes and sowing wallflowers straight into the soil. From her Devon garden, Carol Klein is exploring the latest plant science, uncovering what is really going on inside a seed the moment it is sown, and how this pioneering knowledge can transform the way people garden. Rekha Mistry is also on a mission to grow big in a small space, using only pots on her patio. In Oxfordshire, a garden designed for both beauty and biodiversity shows how plants can support wildlife as well as people. And a viewer in rural France shares a breathtaking, naturalistic plot that blends seamlessly with the surrounding landscape.

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The Mackay family want to make the most of the sunny spot in an unloved corner of the garden in their London home. Their shed is tired and so full they can’t fit anything in, and their bathroom is showing signs of age and limescale. The team construct decking and a pergola so the family can enjoy the sunshine together. The shed is tidied with storage added, and their bathroom is deep cleaned so it gleams.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: From the sublime to the ridiculous - a painting by an Australian war artist, a silver claret jug and two diamond rings contrast with a painting with a large hole through the middle and a permit for carrying a cigarette lighter in Portugal. Michael and the experts visit Leeds Town Hall.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the historic Barrow Hill Roundhouse near Chesterfield in Derbyshire, where experts Jonathan Pratt and Michael Baggott value some of the county's antiques and collectibles. Jonathan falls in love with a Thonet hat and coat stand, and Michael comes across a box of Victorian cut-throat razors which get pulses racing at the auction. Paul Martin takes a trip to the village of Hathersage in the Peak District National Park, which provided inspiration for the novel Jane Eyre.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Nikki Fox, Ruthie Henshall, Danny John-Jules and Ignacio Lopez take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Belgian journey takes him back to Brussels to examine a dark chapter in the country’s past. At the Museum of Africa, on the edge of the city, he learns about Belgium’s brutal seizure of the Congo under King Leopold II and a grand exhibition to celebrate his colonial success. Travelling south into French-speaking Wallonia, Michael visits the site of the Battle of Waterloo, one of Britain’s most famous military victories. He explores a key position at Hougoumont Farm, where Wellington’s soldiers defended themselves from Napoleon’s forces, and joins re-enactors to fire a cannon known as Le Brutal. In the province of Hainaut, the centre of Belgium’s Industrial Revolution, Michael admires a 19th-century boat lift, one of four on the Canal du Centre, the only working examples of their kind in the world today.

programme.title: Scams & Scandals
programme.desc: What happens when the sperm or egg donor you choose isn't the one you get? Northern Cyprus is a sun-soaked haven for affordable IVF. But behind the glossy clinic websites, parents are discovering their chosen sperm or egg donors might not have been used. A BBC investigation follows parents searching for answers and children wondering where they have come from. Details of organisations offering information and support with infertility are available on the pregnancy-related issues page at bbc.co.uk/actionline.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Some more unusual methods of growing are demonstrated at Beechgrove Garden. Ruth Vichos attempts to produce a mushroom crop and there’s a report on some of Scotland’s best bonsai, with everything you need to know to start that form of cultivation. Brian Cunningham is in the Seaside Garden at Beechgrove refreshing the planting with varieties that can withstand a coastal climate and Brian turns conifers into sculptures with topiary. Plus the week’s handy hints.

Whilst the Squirrels fuel up with important breakfasts, Roly’s family are still trying to wake him up. And only the promise of breakfast will do the trick! After freshening up, brushing their teeth and picking out the perfect outfit, the Squirrels start packing the essentials for their walk. They gawk at the amazing sights and interesting characters that they meet along the way, and they even get a magical lift home. It was well worth getting ready for that morning!

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Febo's family are from America, where they celebrate Thanksgiving. As it is traditional on Thanksgiving to prepare and serve pumpkin pie as a dessert, Febo is making this for his friends. He starts by making a pastry case and fitting it into a pie dish. For the pumpkin filling, he pours melted butter and buttermilk into a bowl of brown sugar, along with whisked egg, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, allspice and cloves. Febo adds his special ingredient, pumpkin puree, and then mixes them all together. When it is mixed, he spoons it into the empty pastry case and puts it in the oven to cook. Febo's friends all help to decorate his American-themed table before they taste his pumpkin pie.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Maddie learns what happens to food in our bodies when we eat it and why it’s important to eat a variety of different foods from different food groups. We find out which foods give us energy to move around, which help our bodies grow and repair, and which foods we get vitamins and minerals from. Then Maddie visits a meringue factory where she discovers how the proteins in egg whites work to make the meringue. She uses her special slow-motion camera to see how the giant whisks mix the egg whites with sugar, so that the mixture turns glossy and thick. And we see how the meringue is cooked to make it crunchy on the outside and gooey in the middle.

programme.title: Dog Squad

Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover that these clever camels grow special coats for the winter to keep warm, and shed or lose them for the hotter summer months to stay cool. Their next animal is the super stealthy lynx. This wonderful cat is rarely seen in the wild. This fabulous feline is a fantastic hunter and uses its incredible hearing to catch prey. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po enjoy Tiddlytubbies Songtime. Then it is time for Teletubbies Songtime. The Teletubbies sing solo before singing all together.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how dead wood plays an important role in the environment. They find out that even though the wood is no longer alive, dead wood is a home for animals, insects, birds and fungi, and learn that dead wood breaks down to give nutrients back to the soil. On the way, they have a game of tag by an upright dead tree called a snag!

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: The Fantastics playfully sack Georgie. Jaz is appointed as the team’s new coach but finds it harder than she thought. Georgie tries her hand at other jobs - with chaotic results.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: CBeebies’ very own motorcycle rider Grace shows off three amazing machines that all go downhill! Grace races down a hill on a street luge, then shows up on a cool snow bike before getting to grips with a gravity bike!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: When Ginger gets a nasty tummy ache, the Pea-Rexes have to find a special soothing herb.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When the rabbits find themselves surrounded, Peter is forced to create a brand new ingenious escape route.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are having a picnic and notice that the chickens eat differently than they do. Duggee has his eating badge and can explain all the different ways animals eat. Some animals eat slowly like cows, who eat all day long. But others eat quickly like frogs. Some, like goats, are always eating, while tortoises can go a whole year without food. Some animals eat food that is very high up, like giraffes, and some eat food that is very low down, like moles. The Squirrels finish off their picnic, having learned a lot about all the different ways of eating.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When some exhausted mums arrive at the clinic, Vida knows just what they need to relax.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea captures Supertato, but Carrot finally masters the ultimate flip kick and rescues her.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: Weasy thinks he's ace at skateboarding and decides to teach his daughters and the eaglets some tricks. Weasy quickly realises that one of the eaglets has much more talent than he does. Not wanting to lose his authority, Weasy decides to cheat.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Cap’n Gail’s tall tale of a nine-legged octopus in Lake Swoppiton has everyone panicking. But Mojo and Bo wonder: is the story real, or is Cap’n Gail up to something?

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Judo wants to play in the dirt with Bluey and Bingo, but she’s not supposed to get dirty!

programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Twiggy has a funny tummy on the day of his performance. Nothing the doctors try works, not even the cure for froggy moths! Zog wonders if there is something else bothering Twiggy.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: Andy and Jen discover a meteorite crater on Dino Island. But when a grumpy old Ankylosaurus charges through their camp, taking with it all of Andy’s clothes from the washing line, they head out on an epic adventure to save it from falling into the newly found crater. Along the way, Andy meets a velociraptor and a sleepy T. rex, whose roar he needs to record on his gizmo!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Evie finishes her reading book before school, so she can hand it in and bring a new book home later. Home alone, Waffle makes up a chant and dances around the house to the music. He spots Evie’s reading book! She’s accidentally left it behind and it needs to be handed in today. Waffle doesn’t know what to do. He could take the book to Evie, but he’s banned from school...

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi promises her dads she will go straight to bed while Aunty T babysits. But when Aunty T suggests night-time ice cream, Rafi makes a wish and her bed magically flies them out into Manchester! It’s exciting at first, but soon Rafi becomes sleepy and wants to go home. Suddenly, the wish runs out and the bed drops onto a tree. Luckily, Aunty T uses her umbrella to magic them safely back. Rafi realises bedtime is bedtime for a reason.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran visit the woods, keeping a record of all they find on a journey stick. Looking around, they find lots of fallen flowers, leaves, seeds and bark to decorate their stick. They search a little further and see Isaiah and Joshua have found a hut made of twigs. They go even further into the woods but aren’t sure where they are. Gran Gran has a plan: they can use their journey sticks to retrace their steps! Slowly but surely, they find their way back to all their friends in time for lunch.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. When there's a bread festival in the park, Sarah and Duck find themselves part of an exciting treasure hunt.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Tiny and Small are playing cotton ball, but the game keeps getting interrupted by froglets jumping out of the top hat. This distracts Tiny, and she ends up carelessly flipping the ball into the hat to see where it will go. But when she looks into the hat, she finds there is nothing there. Curious as to where it has gone, she climbs into the hat and finds herself in a world of top hats, where each hat is the portal to a strange new place. She only gets back home with the help of the blobs!

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa enjoy going up and down on a seesaw. A Tweetie flies by doing an upside down barrel roll. They fly up to the Play Tree and go down to land. BaBa does an upside down roly-poly. At Yummy Time, the toast jumps up out of the toaster and falls down to the ground, landing upside down. MeMo and BaBa watch Fungi and Pungi do their upside-down somersaults on Lullaby Lake.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures. Everybody decides to take a ride on the Ninky Nonk. Igglepiggle, Upsy Daisy, Makka Pakka and the teeny tiny Pontipines all get on board the Ninky Nonk. Hurry up Tombliboos! What's that sound? It is the Pinky Ponk! The Tombliboos decide to ride in the Pinky Ponk instead. The Ninky Nonk takes all their friends for a very bouncy ride, what a silly Ninky Nonk! Oh no, it is the ponk alarm - get ready for a ponk, Tombliboos! The Pinky Ponk ponks into a tree and then it ponks into the Gazebo, what a silly Pinky Ponk! The Tombliboos decide to ride on the Ninky Nonk with all their friends instead.

programme.desc: Leah Williamson tells an inspirational tale about the importance of being yourself.

programme.title: Bing

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies get very messy when the Tubby Custard Machine takes them on a Tubby Custard Ride, which splats tubby custard everywhere. The children in Tummy Tales have messy fun with art in the park.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Explore the amazing world around us with baby monkey Tee and his Mum, Mo. Sing along, join in with stories and get ready for some family fun!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: The Veggies are in the middle of working out when Evil Pea interrupts to tell them about her plan to freeze the entire supermarket. She has placed freezy sprinklers all around the aisles! They split up to deactivate the sprinklers before it's too late. But when the Veggies reach them, they realise the sprinklers are fake. Evil Pea is actually getting on with her real, even bigger plan - setting up a giant freezy hose to freeze Tato Tower! The Veggies must now get to Tato Tower in time for Supertato to save the day.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Sula’s cousin Nicky is visiting, something Bing is a little unsure about. Sula and Bing start making 'rippy pictures', and while Sula is looking for some purple paper Bing shows Nicky how to voosh the blue speedy car down the slide. However, Nicky vooshes too, falling and breaking his glasses! Sula is furious and Bing is forlorn. Amma soothes Bing while Nicky shows him that he can click his glasses back together again.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: The cheese delivery race is on as Mojo and the racer top try to deliver food faster than Filo. But the competition gets too hot when an explosive souffle is on the table!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Stunt Mole balances on Ethel’s back as she blows a big question mark with her trunk - what action-packed activities will Duggee be doing in Squirrel Club? First up is a set of wooden pieces that fit together to make Duggee’s head, then it’s time for Story Blocks. Tag runs happily along, Tino introduces us to the art of puppetry, and the Old Deers take a spin through the ages. Finally, Roly recalls a time when he had no teeth, and our real-life Squirrel puppets sing a catchy song about the very best thing: Squirrel Club, of course!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Norrie admits that she can’t ride her new bike because she finds it too difficult. So Duggee gives her some encouragement and lets her know that there are skills that he is still yet to master too, like skateboarding. In fact, each Squirrel has a skill they find difficult. Tag can’t tie his shoe laces, Happy can’t click his fingers, Roly can’t swing and Betty discovers she can’t blink. Now that she is not alone, Norrie agrees to keep trying as Duggee encourages the Squirrels not to quit when things are difficult and that if at first you don’t succeed, try again! Duggee lets them know that when things are hard, you can always ask for help.

programme.desc: Judo wants to play in the dirt with Bluey and Bingo, but she’s not supposed to get dirty!

programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: The Go Jetters are adventure-seeking explorers who soar around the planet fixing environmental problems caused by Grandmaster Glitch!

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter accidentally destroys the squirrels' store of nuts with one of Mr Bouncer's misfiring inventions, he sets off to perilous Owl Island to replace them!

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. When two young leafy sea dragons are accidentally separated from their father and brought onboard the Octopod, the Octonauts must find them before they end up in Kwazii's stew!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Twelve shows the others how to put their blocks into columns and rows - and master the way of the rectangle. Learn about numbers that make rectangle shapes with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. When O and F turn the lights off, how will they get them back on?

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: A sales rep visits. Despite Pancake’s doubts, he convinces the Piris to buy extra flippers. The penguins discover that their purchases are duds but find a clever new use for them.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella and Lift visit the Sing Song Forest, where Tincy the Spider needs help from the Playtimers to wake up her furry friend, Hedge the Hedgehog.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: 'You don't need a lot... just a little bit will do.' At bath time, Bing just cannot help adding a few more squirts of bubble goo, and a few more, until he gets more bubbles than he can handle.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘train’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see lots of different types of train – a long train, a fast train, a slow train and a choo-choo train. There is an animal train, a scrummy train made of food, and everyone has a ride on a miniature train! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Barnaby doesn't like the pressure of choosing between Lu and Biba's games.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri is sad when Lou goes away to a private meeting of his species, the Palorchecies. So she decides to follow him.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button make a clever telescope and enjoy a magical star-filled adventure.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: Stop-motion preschool programme about the adventures of four inquisitive Twirlywoos. Things get out of hand when Chickedy and Chick try to turn the pedals of a bike.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Ben meets Hamidah and Emily at a theatre, where they dress up a character - and themselves! Mr Tumble has some fancy dress fun pretending to be all kinds of different things, including a spaceman, a ballerina and a bunny. The spotty surprise is a fashion show. Featuring signs for the words clothes, dressing up and crown.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po run around in circles in the Home Dome. The Noo-noo joins in and the Teletubbies have fun chasing.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies Marta, Hud, Theo, Isobel, Sehaj, Isaac and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are teddy bears which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate teddy bears inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun song ‘Round and Round the Garden’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Baby Bear Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children weave mulberry bushes on paper plates, learn BSL signs for bush, cold and morning, then sing and sign Here We Go Round the Mulberry Bush.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Allotment gardener Chloe Taylor and the Fact Pack discover how the wind helps sweetcorn plants grow, and just how many little kernels are on one cob. We also learn how yummy popcorn pops!

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca and Murphi are playing hide-and-seek. Murphi is so difficult to find that he comes out of hiding to help Rebecca make a cardboard tube tracker dog. The Mini Monsters make paper bag monsters, and Rebecca’s Grandpa calls to share his fishing frustrations. The Recycling Express brings a shoebox, inspiring a mega monster idea - a magnificent monster! And the Tiny Helpers are on hand to help make the hutch.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Split follows a glowing Chillipede into the Spooky Forest and gets lost in a tree maze.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: When Dad has to stop having fun with the girls and go to work, Bluey and Bingo scramble to keep him playing games with them on the trampoline!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee and the Squirrels have an exciting woodland adventure ahead of them, and everyone has their own routine to prepare for the day. Some are more keen on early starts than others – Happy is ready before his alarm, whereas Roly sleeps right through it. Whilst the Squirrels fuel up with important breakfasts, Roly’s family are still trying to wake him up. And only the promise of breakfast will do the trick! After freshening up, brushing their teeth and picking out the perfect outfit, the Squirrels start packing the essentials for their walk. They gawk at the amazing sights and interesting characters that they meet along the way, and they even get a magical lift home. It was well worth getting ready for that morning!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk along a woodland trail to a place where they can play a game with sticks and stones. On the way they find a tree monster tunnel, make wishes in a wishing well, count shapes in a little building and even fly like owls!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Chef Audrey loves to cook and makes a delicious pizza for the whole family. Later, the family has a game of snakes and ladders. It’s a close-run thing with lots of ups and downs, but who will end up being the champion? After a busy day, Audrey has a bedtime singsong before settling down to sleep.

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Febo's family are from America, where they celebrate Thanksgiving. As it is traditional on Thanksgiving to prepare and serve pumpkin pie as a dessert, Febo is making this for his friends. He starts by making a pastry case and fitting it into a pie dish. For the pumpkin filling, he pours melted butter and buttermilk into a bowl of brown sugar, along with whisked egg, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, allspice and cloves. Febo adds his special ingredient, pumpkin puree, and then mixes them all together. When it is mixed, he spoons it into the empty pastry case and puts it in the oven to cook. Febo's friends all help to decorate his American-themed table before they taste his pumpkin pie.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Maddie learns what happens to food in our bodies when we eat it and why it’s important to eat a variety of different foods from different food groups. We find out which foods give us energy to move around, which help our bodies grow and repair, and which foods we get vitamins and minerals from. Then Maddie visits a meringue factory where she discovers how the proteins in egg whites work to make the meringue. She uses her special slow-motion camera to see how the giant whisks mix the egg whites with sugar, so that the mixture turns glossy and thick. And we see how the meringue is cooked to make it crunchy on the outside and gooey in the middle.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Hearing dog Diesel visits Woofton library to work on Rayane’s homework project, which is all about sound. But when their timer goes missing, Diesel needs his super ears to find it!

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie head out on safari and meet Bactrian camels. In the wild, these incredible animals live in the Gobi Desert, where it gets really hot and really cold. Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover that these clever camels grow special coats for the winter to keep warm, and shed or lose them for the hotter summer months to stay cool. Their next animal is the super stealthy lynx. This wonderful cat is rarely seen in the wild. This fabulous feline is a fantastic hunter and uses its incredible hearing to catch prey. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.desc: Where have all the berries gone? Mossy and Oona are on the case.

programme.desc: Stripes’s attempts to write a song about his love for the Sunhouse are interrupted by the rest of the gang. Can Yukee find a way to help him finish his song?

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs

Igglepiggle, Upsy Daisy, Makka Pakka and the teeny tiny Pontipines all get on board the Ninky Nonk. Hurry up Tombliboos! What's that sound? It is the Pinky Ponk! The Tombliboos decide to ride in the Pinky Ponk instead. The Ninky Nonk takes all their friends for a very bouncy ride, what a silly Ninky Nonk! Oh no, it is the ponk alarm - get ready for a ponk, Tombliboos! The Pinky Ponk ponks into a tree and then it ponks into the Gazebo, what a silly Pinky Ponk! The Tombliboos decide to ride on the Ninky Nonk with all their friends instead.
